1.explanation: 1) Dropdown.js is where the React Dropdown is assembled using Downshift and the ListBox primitives—it passes down props to the ListBoxMenu and ListBoxMenuItem. Any fix for keyboard focus or ARIA attributes ultimately needs to start here or in the passed downshiftProps. 2) ListBoxMenu.js renders the wrapper with role="listbox" but never sets a tabindex (e.g. tabindex="0" or "-1") nor manages aria-activedescendant. Without a focusable container, screen readers and keyboard users cannot focus or interact with the listbox. 3) ListBoxMenuItem.js renders each <li> with role="option" but never adds a tabindex attribute (e.g. tabindex="-1" on inactive items, tabindex="0" on the active one) or makes them intrinsically focusable. That omission leaves no tabbable children, triggering the a11y violation.
1.bug_scenario: When the Dropdown component is opened (either on the Carbon site or in the user’s code), the IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker flags a critical violation: “None of the descendent elements with “option” role is tabbable.” In the DOM you can see a <ul> (or wrapper div) with role="listbox" and many <li role="option">, but neither the container nor the options themselves have any tabindex or are otherwise keyboard-focusable. That means neither the listbox nor its options can receive keyboard focus, causing a WCAG accessibility failure.

2.explanation:
The violation is rooted in the ListBox-based implementation of Dropdown. 

• ListBox.js defines the outer container (role=listbox) and controls focus via aria-activedescendant but does not set a tabindex on the container (or the options), so no element in the list is actually tabbable.

• ListBoxMenu.js renders the <ul> container for the options but does not add any focusable attributes (e.g. tabindex) on the container.

• ListBoxMenuItem.js renders each <li> with role=’option’ but likewise omits tabindex attributes on each option, so individual options are never in the tab sequence.

• Dropdown.js composes the ListBox components into the final <Dropdown> API—so while it passes through props and downshift behavior, it doesn’t modify the focusability of the underlying ListBox elements.

To resolve the violation, the ListBox container or each option item must be made keyboard-focusable (for example by adding tabindex=0 on each <li role="option"> or making the container tabbable and using aria-activedescendant to manage focus). These files must be updated to add the appropriate tabindex or focus management attributes to satisfy automated accessibility checks.
2.bug_scenario: When opening a <Dropdown> on a carbon-react page (v10 or v11), the IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker flags a critical violation under the listbox role: “None of the descendent elements with ‘option’ role is tabbable.” In other words, each <li role=’option’> inside the opened menu cannot receive keyboard focus, so a standard accessibility tool reports that the options themselves aren’t in the tab order.
